name: All I Want for Christmas Is You

info.album: All I Want For Christmas Is You (Mariah's New Dance Mixes 2009)

podcast.body: Mariah Carey's Christmas classic, recorded in 1994, was not released as a single at the time but only as an album cut, a deliberate decision by Carey and Sony Music. Consequently, it was ineligible for the Hot 100 in 1994 and did not chart. Its eventual topping of the Hot 100 a quarter-century later is attributed more to Billboard metrics catching up with its inherent popularity rather than a traditional second chance hit narrative, as the song was always popular. "Here's the thing about Carey's hit. It's not an archetypal second chance hit. Carey's Christmas classic wasn't released as a single in 1994 only an album cut."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: Originally released in 1994, this song is considered the all-time modern holiday song champion, generating an estimated $70 million USD in royalties despite being played only two months a year. It is one of the best-selling singles of all time, not just Christmas singles, and has been covered numerous times by artists across various genres. "Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas is You, which originally came out in 1994."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
